findings.where: the last row of the thread, y=2726-2795 of 3120, directly above the composer
findings.what: The report says the capture was anchored on 'types:voice_note,video at rows 7286 to 7290' and that the eight visible rows include video:1; the voice note renders in full (waveform, 0:47, read checks) but the video row is a torn paper sliver 70 px tall at x=600 containing no poster frame, no play control, no duration, no timestamp and no delivery mark, and its layout box (the grey outline at x=130-1230) runs past the paper it was given.
findings.why: The rubric requires video to be present and dependable; the one artifact in evidence that deliberately scrolled to a video message shows nothing of it, and 'video' appears nowhere else in evidence except the attach-sheet string in logs/strings.json, so a video message is unevidenced as a thing either person can actually watch.

findings.where: the reply preview above the composer, y=2650-2700 of 3120
findings.what: The log records replying_to 0001M4ZQQ0H0PPVTKMMQEE268D, and the screen renders that reply target as the literal string 'answering state_declared' - a raw internal type slug with an underscore - at a measured contrast of 1.35:1 against the wood behind it (computed from sRGB relative luminance, ink at p98 = 0.1554, ground at p25 = 0.1023).
findings.why: Replies are a named capability; a reply chip that names the machine's word for the event kind instead of quoting the message, and does so at 1.35:1 where it cannot be read at all, means neither person can tell what they are about to reply to - a reply sent blind is exactly the failure that sends someone back to a messenger that quotes properly.

findings.where: per_frame, 809 frames of the 11_chat_scroll fling at 360x780 dpr 3
findings.what: Build cost is bimodal, not uniformly slow: 243 of 809 frames (30.0%) cost 938-1651 ms to build (median 1134 ms) while the other 566 cost a median of 14 ms, and the heavy frames recur on a fixed cadence - the modal gap between them is exactly 3 frames (173 of 242 gaps), with 96.7% of all build time (283,567 of 293,356 ms) spent in them. Raster is flat by comparison (p50 164 ms, p95 188 ms, max 226 ms), so the spike is CPU-side rebuild work, not the absent GPU.
findings.why: The rubric names 'no scroll jank against the year-deep seeded history'; a full rebuild costing 81x an ordinary frame every third frame of a fling is that jank, and it is the only timing evidence that can show it, because 11_chat_scroll.mp4 is assembled one grabbed frame per 16 ms clock step and therefore cannot render a hitch no matter how long the frame took to build.

findings.where: the composer row; in 02_chat.png the nearest paper ends at y=2795 of 3120 and the controls sit at y=2820-2900
findings.what: The composer's paper surface is a 70 px empty strip that its own contents overflow: the attach glyph, the placeholder 'write something', the voice glyph and 'send' are all painted on bare wood below it, with a ruled blue line from the paper continuing across the wood. 'send' measures 3.65:1 and the placeholder 3.67:1 against the wood, against 8.11:1 for body text on paper in the same image. In 13_messenger_states.png the composer has no paper at all - draft, attach row and send all float on the desk. The same defect is in 11_chat_scroll.mp4 from 14:29 and still in 02_chat.png recaptured at 18:24, so it is not transient.
findings.why: Send is the single most-used control in a messenger; a send affordance with no surface, no boundary and less than half the contrast of the message text is a control the couple has to hunt for on every message.

findings.where: the attach sheet, 'a photo  take one  a video  film something', y=2735-2785 of 3120
findings.what: With attaching:true in the log, the four attachment choices render as dark handwriting directly on the wood grain with no surface, no separation and no hit boundary, measured at 2.05:1 (ink p2 = 0.0425, ground p75 = 0.1397), and they overlap the reply preview immediately above them.
findings.why: This sheet is the entire entry point to photos, video and voice notes; below 3:1 even as large text, on top of a high-frequency wood pattern, the multimedia half of the messenger is behind a control the reader can barely see.

findings.where: the filter list, y=245 to y=955 of 1170 in the screen, and the single result below it
findings.what: Searching 'rain' across the 14,062-event archive puts twelve full-width torn filter strips (EVERYTHING, WRITTEN, PHOTOGRAPHS, VIDEO, TALKING, FEELINGS, DATES, THE LIST, STATE, NOOR, TEO, THIS YEAR) between the query and the results - about 62% of the screen - and leaves exactly one hit visible, clipped by the tab bar. The twelve strips are visually indistinguishable: mean grey over each strip's text band spans only 218.1 to 224.8 out of 255, so no selected scope can be read off the screen. There is no result count anywhere.
findings.why: 'Full-text and media search' is a named capability and searchable history is one of the mission's stated reasons for leaving Instagram; a search that shows one hit, no count and no legible active filter over a year of messages is not a searchable history in practice, however well logs/reliability.json's search check indexes nine event types.

findings.where: every delivery marker in every artifact, and the missing block of MANIFEST.json
findings.what: The only delivery state that appears anywhere is 'read' with two checks. No artifact shows a sent-but-undelivered, queued or failed message, although logs/strings.json carries 'waiting to send' (app/lib/voice/strings.dart:23) and "can't reach the other phone. it'll go when it can." (line 48). Every messenger scene was captured with link 'connected' and sync.pending 0 (01_pulse through 15_authored_feeling), and 09_two_devices.png is absent from MANIFEST.json with the reason 'not captured this session'.
findings.why: The rubric asks whether the delivery and read marker can be trusted and whether ordering after a reconnect is right; with a single visible state, no picture of the link down, no picture of a queued message and no two-device artifact at all, 'delivery state' exists only as prose in reliability.json - a person cannot tell an unsent message from a delivered one in anything a critic can see.

findings.where: the lower-right corner of the note 'two stops. put the kettle on the second one not the first one', around x=1050-1250, y=1200-1330
findings.what: The only candidate reaction in any artifact is an unlabelled flat grey folded-paper object with a drop shadow attached to a note corner. It carries no name, no count and no attribution, the per-region report has no reactions field at all, and visually identical grey folded objects appear inside message bodies elsewhere (11_chat_scroll.mp4 frame 1, the 'thinking of you' and 'goodnight' notes), so a reaction cannot be told apart from message content.
findings.why: Reactions are a named capability; reliability.json asserts one folded onto its target on the host, but nothing in the pictures lets either person read which reaction was given or by whom, which is the whole point of a reaction.

findings.where: the top-level transport field, the tailscale block, and both later_check blocks
findings.what: All eighteen capability checks - including the offline queue, reconnect ordering and kill-mid-send - ran with transport 'local' over 127.0.0.1:34683 at latency_ms 0. The tailnet evidence is a separate four-event exchange dated 2026-09-05T00:28:41Z, and both reliability.json's tailscale.later_check and coldstart.json's later_check read status 'pending', 'the nodes were not answering when this was re-run'.
findings.why: The rubric's reconnect and ordering clause is about the link the couple will really use; a zero-latency loopback with scripted faults cannot show what reordering or duplication a real tailnet reconnect produces, and the one tailnet run in evidence carries four events, not the 174 the loopback run carries.

findings.what: A first launch that imports the seeded year costs 12,363 ms (02_chat), 12,289 ms (01_pulse) and 12,577 ms (07_feeling_landing) with store 'fresh', against 2,487-2,739 ms for every 'kept' launch. No artifact in evidence shows what is on screen during those twelve seconds.
findings.why: 'No spinner that outstays its welcome' is a named clause; twelve seconds is well past welcome, and with no capture of the loading state a critic cannot tell whether the couple sees progress, a stalled screen, or nothing at all.

what_is_working: reliability.json's eighteen capability checks all pass with 174 events on each side, duplicates 0, ordering monotonic and same_order_both_sides true, after a lost response and two offline/online cycles were injected.

The hard reliability cases are covered and pass: 26 events queued offline and all delivered on reconnect, client seq 1..173 gapless and monotonic after the gap, a kill mid-send received once with the retry not duplicating it, the host's own outbox delivered with its sequence intact, and a draft plus the pairing surviving the client process being closed and reopened.

13_messenger_states.png shows four states legibly on paper in one frame: 'read' with two checks, an 'edited' mark with its revision glyph, a deleted message as the stub 'took this back' rather than a hole in the thread, and the typing indicator 'noor writing...'.

02_chat.png renders a voice note properly in the thread - play triangle, drawn waveform, duration 0:47, timestamp and read marker - and 04_moments.png shows further voice notes as durations (21s, 38s, 41s, 47s, 63s).

Ordering through the dense scroll is correct: stepping 11_chat_scroll.mp4 frame by frame, timestamps rise monotonically from 'Wed 22 Apr 21:40' to 'Mon 27 Apr', with no message appearing twice and frames.json reporting repeated_frames 0 over all 300 frames.

The rendered scroll itself is clean: measuring per-frame vertical displacement by phase correlation over frames 1-300 gives seven flings that each decelerate monotonically from about 100 to 22 device px per frame, with no zero-delta frame (minimum |dy| = 22.18 px), no backward step, and per-ramp acceleration never below -0.93 px per frame squared.

14_media_viewer.png shows a real photograph whole - 1351 x 1340 px inside a 1440-wide frame, with margins on both sides rather than a crop - and reliability.json's viewer check confirms the full-resolution bytes on the far device hash to the same blob.

04_moments.png's log reports 183 media items with 26 tiles built and blobs asked 18 / arrived 18 / reading 0 / waiting 0, and the artifact shows every tile filled - no stalled or placeholder thumbnails against the year of history.
Search does highlight its hit in place: 'rain' is picked out in the result 'it's raining here too. the canal has gone all dimples', with the message's own date beneath it.
verdict: The spine of this messenger is real and, where it is measured rather than pictured, genuinely dependable: 174 events on both sides with zero duplicates, gapless monotonic ordering after two disconnections and a lost response, 26 events queued offline and all delivered, a send killed mid-flight that arrives exactly once, and a draft that survives the process dying. Text, read state, editing, deletion, typing and voice notes are all visible on screen, the year-deep list scrolls with no repeated or reversed frames, and the media grid fills every tile. What is missing is everything on the other side of that spine. Video, a named capability, is never once shown rendered in a thread - the single capture that deliberately anchored on a video row (logs/02_chat.report.json, rows 7286-7290) shows it as a 70 px empty sliver with no poster, no duration and no play control. The reply affordance names its target 'answering state_declared', a raw type slug, at 1.35:1 against the wood. The composer's contents have fallen off their own paper in both the newest still and the scroll clip, leaving 'send' at 3.65:1 on bare wood, and the attach sheet that leads to photo, video and voice sits at 2.05:1 with no surface at all. Search over 14,062 events spends 62% of the screen on twelve indistinguishable filter strips and surfaces one hit with no count. And the only timing evidence that can show jank - logs/scroll_webkit.json, since the clip is grabbed one frame per clock step and cannot show a hitch - reports a 1,134 ms median rebuild on every third frame of the fling against a 14 ms median otherwise, 96.7% of all build time in 30% of the frames, with raster flat throughout, so it is not the missing GPU. Any one of the reply chip, the invisible attach sheet, the unshowable video or the third-frame rebuild is a reason to open Instagram instead; four of them together, plus a delivery state that only ever says 'read' and a missing 09_two_devices.png, put this category below its floor.
